verdict: Amgen's revenue rose 8% to $10.4B as more patients used its medicines, and a $1.5B paper gain on its investment stakes helped lift net income to $3.9B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $5.93 a year ago; non-GAAP was $6.45

kpis.label: Equity-investment gains
kpis.note: Paper gains inside other income — not from selling medicines

segments.name: Product sales
segments.note: Sales of Amgen's medicines — brands such as Repatha, Prolia, Evenity and Tepezza — up 8% on higher volumes.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Royalties and other partnership income, up 15%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines and running clinical trials — up 11% as the pipeline expanded.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling medicines and running the company.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Smaller operating items, down sharply from $329M a year ago.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $1,629M — including $1,465M of gains on equity investments Amgen holds — less $653M of net interest expense.

takeaways.title: Volume, not price, drove growth
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 8% to $10.4B, and product sales rose 8% entirely on volume — more prescriptions and patients — rather than price rises. Cost of sales actually fell 10% as the product mix improved.

takeaways.title: A paper gain flattered the bottom line
takeaways.text: Net income jumped 20% to $3.9B, but $1,465M of it came from mark-to-market gains on equity investments Amgen owns, booked in other income. On the company's non-GAAP view, which strips those out, earnings were $3.5B.

takeaways.title: Research spending keeps climbing
takeaways.text: R&D rose 11% to $2.1B as Amgen funds late-stage trials, including its closely watched weight-loss program. SG&A was roughly flat, so most of the quarter's extra revenue dropped through to operating income, up 47%.

oneTimers: Other income includes $1,465M of net gains from equity investments — paper (non-cash) gains from marking Amgen's stakes in partner companies to market value. They can reverse in any quarter; Amgen's non-GAAP results exclude them.
